prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map separates the foreground workspace—where the camera wearer's left and right hands (~0.2–0.4 m away) and a second person's head and head-mounted action camera (~0.3–0.5 m away) appear bright white-grey in the lower half of frames 1–4—from the darker grey-to-black sloping hillside terrain rising behind and above them from roughly 1.5 m to over 20 m away. Across frames 1 to 4, both hands remain within arm's reach (~0.0–0.15 m from the action camera and head strap), with the right hand reaching over the action camera from the right to partially occlude it in frames 1 and 3 while the left hand holds the strap on the lower left, and most of the second person's head and torso cut off below the bottom frame edge. In frame 5, the second person is positioned slightly farther back (~0.5–0.8 m) in the centre-left foreground facing right in profile and looking away from the camera wearer, while the camera wearer's left hand rests at ~0.3 m on the person's back shoulder and the right hand drops out of view. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map makes the sharp metric step between the near-field hands/headgear and the camouflaged, textured vegetation behind them immediately obvious, as well as the continuous upward slope of the background hill. However, depth is unreliable where foreground bright values saturate on the closest left hand in frames 2–4 (losing surface relief between fingers and head) and along the fuzzy fur-hood trim in frame 5.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates foreground actors and objects on a black background, locating the camera wearer's left and right hands in the lower left and right of frames 1–4 (~0.2–0.4 m from the viewpoint) right next to the action camera and mount (~0.3–0.5 m away) on the top of the second person's head just below them. Across frames 1–4, the masks show the left hand on the lower left and the right hand moving from grasping the camera in frame 1, pulling back to the lower right edge in frame 2, touching the right side of the camera in frame 3, and opening slightly to the right in frame 4, before frame 5 shows the second person upright in right profile (~0.5–0.8 m away, facing right and not looking at the camera wearer) with only the camera wearer's left hand visible at the bottom-left touching their shoulder. While this map clearly delineates boundaries between the overlapping hands, head, and mounted camera device that blend together against dark hair and shadow in the RGB strip, it omits the entire background hillside layout. It is also heavily unreliable in class and instance consistency: the head-mounted action camera is mislabelled as a 'cell phone' in frames 2–4 and merged into the person mask in frames 1 and 5, the second person's head is completely missed in frames 1–3, and the camera wearer's arms are fragmented into multiple overlapping 'person' instances in frames 3 and 4.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders sparse 2D joint skeletons on a black background, showing only close-range upper-body and hand keypoints within ~0.2–0.8 m of the camera wearer and providing no information about the background terrain or non-human objects. In frame 1, a magenta hand skeleton and an erroneous yellow arm/face skeleton appear at the camera wearer's right hand (~0.3 m away, above and right of the action camera), while frame 2 contains no detected skeletons at all despite both hands and the other person's head being present in the lower foreground. In frames 3 and 4, a single magenta hand skeleton tracks the camera wearer's right hand in the lower-right foreground (~0.3 m away) and then the left hand on the left side of the second person's head (~0.25 m away), both within arm's reach of the headgear. In frame 5, yellow facial keypoints (eye, ear, nose) and a single yellow shoulder-to-elbow line capture the second person at ~0.5–0.8 m in the centre-left facing right in profile and looking away from the camera wearer, with the lower torso occluded below the frame. Compared to RGB, the pose map explicitly localizes individual finger phalanges during close manipulation and confirms the second person's rightward head orientation in frame 5, but it is highly unreliable due to missing most visible hands across frames 1–5, hallucinating a miniature body skeleton inside the right hand in frame 1, and failing to detect the second person in frames 1–4.
